s: a medieval restaurant in a 13th-century wine cellar under Old Riga
w: A restaurant built into a 13th-century wine cellar first recorded in 1293 as the Riga City Council's own festival hall and wine vault. Five candlelit stone halls hold the city's only surviving well and a fragment of Riga's first defensive wall, built in 1201; recipes follow old Latvian and medieval European sources, honey mead included.
_facts: Located at Rozena iela 1, Vecrīga (Old Riga), LV-1050
Housed in a 13th-century wine cellar first documented in 1293 as the Riga City Council's festival hall
Contains Riga's only surviving well and a fragment of the city's original 1201 defensive wall
Serves dishes based on medieval and traditional Latvian recipes across five halls seating up to 150

s: a windmill-topped, log-cabin leisure centre serving self-service Latvian classics to 1,000 at once
w: A sprawling log-cabin building topped with its own windmill, holding one of the Baltics' largest self-service restaurants -- soup served in a hollowed bread loaf, pork, potatoes and pickles carried cafeteria-style past counter after counter. Cheap, hearty, and built for families rather than photographs.
_facts: Located at Krasta iela 76, Latgales priekšpilsēta, Riga LV-1019
Self-service Latvian restaurant and leisure centre in a log-cabin building topped with a windmill
One of the largest eateries in the Baltics, seating up to 1,000 guests
Known for traditional Latvian dishes including soup served in bread

s: a specialty roaster's espresso bar and shop in Old Riga
w: The Old Town outpost of KALVE, a Riga-founded specialty coffee roaster built by a team of Q Grader-certified coffee professionals. Precise espresso and retail bags of the house roast in a small, focused space among Vecrīga's older cafés and restaurants.
_facts: Located at Zigfrīda Annas Meierovica bulvāris 10, Vecrīga, Riga
Espresso Room concept from KALVE Coffee Roasters, a Riga-based specialty coffee company
KALVE holds B Corp certification and employs Q Grader-certified coffee professionals
One of several KALVE locations across Riga, including a flagship roastery on Stabu iela

s: a natural-wine bistro built on Lithuanian seasons and storytelling
w: Chef Martynas Praškevičius opened Džiaugsmas ("joy") in 2017, three years after conceiving it as a bistro and natural wine bar built entirely around Lithuania's four seasons. Simple, organic, locally grown ingredients turn into dishes with a story behind each one -- rye bread under a veil of lard, potato-skin ice cream -- served with an emphasis on approachable pleasure rather than technique for its own sake.
_facts: Located at Vilniaus g. 28, Vilnius LT-01402, Senamiestis (Old Town)
Opened in 2017 by chef Martynas Praškevičius
Bistro and natural wine bar built around seasonal, organic, locally grown Lithuanian ingredients
Repeatedly ranked in the 30 Best Restaurants Lithuania list

s: a Michelin Green Star restaurant serving turnip in place of steak
w: A café by day and restaurant by night in Vilnius's up-and-coming Naujamiestis, run by chef Tadas Eidukevičius on a strict house-made-everything, low-impact ethos -- a buttery soft turnip in fermented rye-bread-beer sauce standing in for meat, malted rye bread and cured mackerel that nod to the chef's childhood summers on the Baltic coast. Holds a Michelin star and a Green Star for sustainability.
_facts: Located at T. Ševčenkos g. 16A, Vilnius, Naujamiestis
Run by chef Tadas Eidukevičius
Holds a Michelin star (since 2024) and a Michelin Green Star (2025) for sustainable practice
Known for house-made everything, including malted rye bread and cured mackerel

s: New York-style bagels reviving a Polish-Jewish Vilnius tradition
w: A small bagel shop on Literatų gatvė bringing the dense, chewy, boiled-then-baked bagel back to a city where it originated centuries ago among Vilnius's Jewish community, before all but disappearing. Bookshelves and a relaxed soundtrack fill a cosy Old Town room that's become a local landmark in its own right.
_facts: Located at Literatų g. 7, Senamiestis (Old Town), Vilnius
Has a second location inside Halės Market on Pylimo g.
Revives the bagel's historic roots among Vilnius's pre-war Jewish community
Known for crispy-chewy, New York-style bagels

s: a former Tsarist-era blacksmith's serving honest, seasonal Estonian and Slavic dishes
w: A restaurant occupying a former Tsarist-era blacksmith's building, now part of the Telliskivi Creative City complex, running on a self-described "simple, honest, local and sustainable" mantra. The seasonally changing menu leans into flavourful Slavic and Estonian dishes rather than minimalist Nordic restraint.
_facts: Relocated to Telliskivi 60-4, 10412 Tallinn in June 2025
Housed in a former Tsarist-era blacksmith's building within Telliskivi Creative City
Recognised in the Michelin Guide
Menu built on local, sustainable, seasonally changing Slavic and Estonian dishes

s: a seafront restaurant pairing a Bib Gourmand bistro with a Michelin-starred hall next door
w: A seafront building in Pirita housing two restaurants under one roof and one team: NOA, a Michelin Bib Gourmand modern European bistro, and NOA Chef's Hall, its Michelin-starred fine-dining sibling next door. Floor-to-ceiling views over the water give both rooms a sense of occasion well beyond central Tallinn's older dining scene.
_facts: Located at Ranna tee 3, 12112 Tallinn, Pirita, on the seafront
Comprises two adjoining restaurants: NOA (Michelin Bib Gourmand) and NOA Chef's Hall (Michelin-starred)
Known for modern European and contemporary fine-dining cuisine with sea views
